text:
jordan-customer: Hey, since our nightly key rotation yesterday our production workers started getting a bunch of 401s to /v1/generate. Dashboard shows the new service key active but the pod logs still show invalid_api_key errors. Any ideas?

mike-support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact curl you used and the response body (redact keys)? Also which deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private)?

sara-cs: tagging for context: customer is on Dedicated in eu-west-1, committed capacity. They rotated via the console at 02:10 UTC.

jordan-customer: Dedicated eu-west-1. Here's sanitized repro from one of the workers:```curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' https://inference.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'```Response:```{ "error": { "type": "invalid_api_key", "message": "API key expired or malformed" } }```

mike-support: Thanks. Two quick guesses: 1) the worker is still using an old cached token (service process caching credentials), or 2) there's a regional binding / org-binding mismatch where the new key was issued for hosted vs dedicated (rare but we've seen it). Can infra check instance-level caches and node agent?

alex-infra: looking at the node agent logs around rotation time we see the rotation hook fired but the agent returned 202 and didn't pull the new secret successfully. Agent log snippet: ```[2024-09-20T02:11:05Z] rotation-hook: start
[2024-09-20T02:11:06Z] rotation-hook: request STS to mint scoped token -> 202 Accepted
[2024-09-20T02:11:06Z] rotation-hook: polling token status -> pending
[2024-09-20T02:15:12Z] rotation-hook: final status -> failed (mint_timeout)```

sara-cs: aha — that explains it. The key was created in the control plane, but the node agent never finished minting the node-level token, so pods kept the previous (now revoked) credential. Jordan, can you confirm if restarting the pod picks up the new key (quick test)?

jordan-customer: Restarted one replica, that one works now (no 401). The rest still failing. We can't restart all at once. Is there a safe rolling fix?

mike-support: Two options: 1) trigger a rolling restart of the deployment (recommended if you can tolerate small restart), 2) manually call the node agent endpoint to re-pull secrets for specific nodes. We can also attempt to re-run rotation hook to force minting. Which would you prefer?

alex-infra: note: there's a built-in endpoint on the node agent `/internal/refresh-credentials` that accepts a POST and will re-attempt STS minting for that node. Example: `curl -X POST http://node-agent:8080/internal/refresh-credentials` — returns 200 on success. We'll help run that for affected nodes.

jordan-customer: Can you run it for us on node-7 and node-9? We can't access node agents from our side.

alex-infra: Running now... node-7 -> 200, node-9 -> 202 then 200. Logs show new token minted and cached.

mike-support: Great. After that, any pods on those nodes should pick up credentials within the next 30s. Jordan, can you confirm requests from those pods succeed?

jordan-customer: Confirmed: node-7 and node-9 replicas now return 200 and proper responses. No more invalid_api_key from those. Rolling restart still scheduled for remaining nodes later tonight. Thanks.

sara-cs: For follow-up, we'll: 1) file an internal ticket to improve rotation-hook retry/mint timeout handling, 2) add a runbook step to check node-agent mint status when dashboard rotation shows partial success, and 3) notify customers when rotation doesn't fully propagate.

mike-support: Also adding a short-term mitigation: when rotation is triggered, we now recommend running a cluster-level refresh job that calls `/internal/refresh-credentials` on all nodes to avoid partial propagation — we'll draft the CLI helper.

jordan-customer: Appreciate the quick help, that saved a lot of heads-down time. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deployment/rotation-hook-monitor reported incident resolved for rotation id rot-20240920-0210 on cluster eu-west-1
